note: The A1 teaching order, hand-written. Read docs/CURRICULUM.md before changing it — the order is the design, not a list.

units.title: Hallo!
canDo: greet someone at any time of day
say thank you, please and sorry
units.grammarNote: None on purpose. Day one is sounds and set phrases; a rule needs words to act on.

units.title: Das Alphabet
canDo: spell your own name out loud
units.grammarNote: ä ö ü ß, and the letters whose German name catches an English speaker out: e, i, j, v, w, y, z.

units.title: Zahlen 0–20
canDo: understand a number said to you
units.grammarNote: Numbers are vocabulary at this size. The teens reverse in the next unit, so they are learnt flat first.

units.title: Wie heißt du?
canDo: say your name and ask for someone else's
units.grammarNote: du/Sie before any verb table, because every sentence after this has to pick one. All of ich/du/er/sie/es/Sie land here: the unit that teaches the pronouns cannot teach three of them.

units.title: Woher kommst du?
units.grammarNote: The verb sits second. Introduced here, on statements only — questions come in unit 19.

units.title: Der, die, das
canDo: use the right article for the words you know
recognise the endings that predict gender
units.grammarNote: THE unit this course was missing. Not a list to memorise: -ung -heit -keit -schaft are die, -chen -lein are das, -er -ling are usually der. Every noun from here on is taught with its article, never bare.

units.title: Was ist das?
canDo: say you do not know a word
units.grammarNote: Practice for unit 6 with objects you can point at. 'Wie heißt das auf Deutsch?' is the sentence that unlocks every later one.

units.title: Sein und haben
canDo: say what you are and what you have
units.grammarNote: The two irregular verbs before the regular pattern, because they are irregular and they are unavoidable.

units.title: Zahlen bis 100
units.grammarNote: einundzwanzig — units before tens, said backwards to an English ear. Needs sein/haben from unit 8 to say anything with it.

units.title: Wie spät ist es?
units.grammarNote: Both systems: halb drei means half past TWO, which is the single most expensive misunderstanding in beginner German. Needs numbers to 60.

units.title: Die Woche
canDo: name the days and parts of the day
talk about today, tomorrow and yesterday
units.grammarNote: am Montag, um acht, im Januar — the three time prepositions, learnt as a set because they are chosen by the kind of time word.

units.title: Verben im Präsens
canDo: say what you do every day
units.grammarNote: -e -st -t -en -t -en. Deferred to unit 12 so there are verbs worth conjugating and a du/Sie decision already made. wir and ihr arrive here, with the two endings that need them.

units.title: Meine Familie
canDo: name the people in your family
units.grammarNote: mein/dein/sein/ihr in the nominative only. The full paradigm waits for unit 38, after the cases exist.

units.title: Plural
canDo: form the plural of the nouns you know
units.grammarNote: -e -er -n/-en -s and no ending. Taught as patterns with their gender tendencies rather than as one exception per word.

units.title: Essen und Trinken
canDo: say what you like and do not like
units.grammarNote: ich möchte as a fixed form, not yet as a modal. It is the politest thing a beginner can own.

units.title: Im Café
canDo: understand what the waiter asks you
units.grammarNote: First unit where the German comes back at you. Uses only units 1–15.

units.title: Nicht und kein
canDo: say something is not the case
say you do not have something
units.grammarNote: kein negates a noun, nicht negates everything else. One rule, and it is the whole of A1 negation.

units.title: Farben und Sachen
canDo: describe an object so somebody finds it
units.grammarNote: Only predicative — das Auto ist rot. Adjective endings before a noun are a B-level headache and are not A1.1.

units.title: Fragen stellen
units.grammarNote: W-word first, or verb first for yes/no. Held until unit 19 so the statement order from unit 5 is solid enough to be broken deliberately.

units.title: Mein Tag
canDo: describe your normal day in order
say when you do each thing
units.grammarNote: Consolidation. Nothing new — everything from units 1–19 in one connected piece of speech.

units.title: Der Akkusativ
canDo: use den, die, das and die as objects
say what you see, have and need
units.grammarNote: The first case shift, and the whole of A1.2 leans on it. Only der becomes den — saying that plainly removes most of the fear.

units.title: Einkaufen
canDo: ask for an amount of something
units.grammarNote: Accusative where you actually meet it: ich nehme den Käse.

units.title: Wo ist das?
canDo: understand left, right and straight on
units.grammarNote: Static place prepositions only. The two-way ones wait for unit 39, after the dative exists.

units.title: In der Stadt
canDo: name the places in a town
units.grammarNote: zum/zur as fixed forms. They are contractions of a dative that has not been taught, and pretending otherwise would be a lie a learner catches later.

units.title: Können und müssen
canDo: say what you have to do
put the second verb at the end
units.grammarNote: The bracket — modal second, infinitive last — is the structural idea of German. Two modals first, not all six.

units.title: Wollen, möchten, dürfen
canDo: tell the difference between wollen and möchten
units.grammarNote: möchten becomes a modal here, having been a fixed phrase since unit 15. Ich will can sound blunt to a German ear; that is worth saying out loud.

units.title: Trennbare Verben
canDo: use a separable verb in a sentence
put the prefix at the end
units.grammarNote: Straight after the modal bracket, because it is the same idea: the meaningful part goes last.

units.title: Die Wohnung
canDo: name the rooms and the furniture
say what is in a room
units.grammarNote: es gibt takes the accusative, which is unit 21 doing real work.

units.title: Der Dativ
canDo: use dem, der and den as indirect objects
say who you give something to
units.grammarNote: The second case, eight units after the first. Introduced through people rather than through a table.

units.title: Termine machen
canDo: make an appointment on the phone
units.grammarNote: The first Alltag-shaped unit. Uses time from unit 10, days from 11, modals from 25.

units.title: Beim Arzt
canDo: name the parts of the body
units.grammarNote: mir tut der Kopf weh — dative where German insists on it and English does not.

units.title: Perfekt mit haben
canDo: form the participle of a regular verb
units.grammarNote: The spoken past, and the third use of the bracket. ge- -t for regular verbs; the strong ones are learnt as they come.

units.title: Perfekt mit sein
units.grammarNote: Movement and change of state take sein. A short closed list, so it is worth learning as a list.

units.title: Das Wetter
canDo: say what the weather is doing
units.grammarNote: A vocabulary breather between the two past tenses and the harder second half.

units.title: Kleidung
units.grammarNote: Still predicative. Attributive endings are deliberately not A1 and the course says so rather than half-teaching them.

units.title: Unterwegs
units.grammarNote: mit dem Bus — the dative from unit 29 in the phrase you use every day.

units.title: Der Imperativ
units.grammarNote: du, ihr and Sie forms. The Sie form is what you meet on signs and in offices, so it comes first here.

units.title: Possessivartikel
canDo: say whose something is in any case
use mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser correctly
units.grammarNote: The full paradigm, now that nominative, accusative and dative all exist. Unit 13 taught the nominative alone; this closes it.

units.title: Wechselpräpositionen
canDo: choose accusative or dative after in, auf, an
say where something is and where it goes
units.grammarNote: The hardest thing in A1 and correctly last: it needs both cases and the wo/wohin distinction. Movement takes the accusative, position the dative.

units.title: Über mich
canDo: introduce yourself for a minute without stopping
say what you did and what you are going to do
ask somebody the same questions back
units.grammarNote: Nothing new. If the forty units worked, this is the unit where you notice.
